summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma on chemotherapy, was readmitted with fever and found to have recurrent E. coli bacteremia. Initial evaluation revealed no abdominal pain, but elevated liver enzymes prompted an ERCP, which identified a blocked bile duct. A plastic stent was removed and metal stents cleaned. Due to persistent obstruction, a percutaneous transhepatic biliary drain (PTC drain) was placed, with pus noted, confirming cholangitis. Microbiology revealed the E. coli strain was resistant to ertapenem, necessitating a switch to IV meropenem for a 10-day course. He remained afebrile, with improving labs, and was discharged home with IV antibiotics via PICC line, oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis, and instructions for drain care. Follow-up was arranged with oncology and interventional radiology.
